misconceptions.claim: A rate k (s^-1) is the probability of the event happening in one unit of time (e.g. k=0.1/s means a 10% chance per second).
misconceptions.truth: A rate is probability per unit time only in the dt→0 limit (hazard): P(event in dt) = k dt. Over a finite interval Δt the probability is 1-e^{-kΔt}, which is ≈ kΔt only when kΔt ≪ 1.

evidence.note: Picked 'probability exactly 0.1 per 1 s' at 100% confidence during probe.
Review 2026-10-11: for k=0.5/s gave 1−e^{−0.5}≈0.39 unprompted and explained the shrinking pool / thin slices.

misconceptions.claim: A rate k = 0.1/s means the event has probability exactly 0.1 per second
misconceptions.truth: k·dt is the probability only over a tiny dt, applied to survivors; over 1 s the probability is 1 − e^(−k) ≈ 0.095

evidence.note: Unprompted (after one hint): saw 1% of a shrinking pool gives more than 900 left.
Correctly applied k·dt per slice to the current survivor pool across three slices.

misconceptions.claim: The density k·e^(−kt) evaluated at t is the probability of having exchanged by time t
misconceptions.truth: k·e^(−kt) is probability per unit time; P(exchanged by t) = 1 − e^(−kt), which is ≤ 1

evidence.note: Answered P(0.1 s) = 10/e > 1; earlier wrote density as e^(-3t) without k.
Unprompted: "it's a density so they must integrate", integrated k e^{−kt} from 0 to 0.2 to get 1 − e^{−1} ≈ 0.63.
Correctly described f(0.4)·dt as the probability of exchanging within [0.4, 0.41], explicitly not "by 0.4".

misconceptions.claim: The survival fraction S in dS/dt = -kS is entropy, and a change in entropy is a probability
misconceptions.truth: S is just the fraction of sites still unexchanged; the k·dt rule is the definition of a rate, unrelated to entropy

evidence.note: Twice this session: 's is entropy, divide by z'; 'a change in entropy IS a probability'. Likely triggered by the letter S. Use U(t) next time.

misconceptions.claim: To chain slices, multiply the per-slice exchange probability k·dt by itself
misconceptions.truth: Multiply the per-slice survival factors (1 − k·dt); exchanged = 1 − product

evidence.note: Correct with concrete 0.5^3 counts, reverted in abstract explain-back at 100% confidence.
Unprompted used 0.95^3 for survivors and 400 − U for exchanged.
Explained unprompted that the product arises because each slice's k·dt acts on the population the previous slice left.

misconceptions.claim: The diagonal entry Q_ii of the rate matrix is the rate of jumping from state i back into state i.
misconceptions.truth: Q_ii = minus the total exit rate from i; it comes from (P_ii − 1)/dt, so rows of Q sum to zero. Staying is not a jump and has no rate.

evidence.note: Review 2026-10-12, 100% confidence; picked −4 correctly afterwards but at 0% confidence.
Wrote full Q for C⇌O→X unprompted with O diagonal −55 = −(50+5) and X row (0,0,0), 100% conf, correct.
Wrote Q for C⇌O→X unprompted with Q_OO = -(30+70) = -100 and used it as the total exit rate from O.

misconceptions.claim: The quasi-steady-state approximation dO/dt ≈ 0 is justified by k_op ≪ k_cl (the open population being small).
misconceptions.truth: It is justified by the total exit rate from O, k_cl + k_ch, being ≫ k_op: O relaxes to its balance much faster than C changes. Smallness of O is a separate (population) statement; which exit is larger (k_cl vs k_ch) decides EX1/EX2, not the approximation.

evidence.note: Review 2026-10-17/18: first attempt compared k_ch vs k_cl and concluded dO/dt not ≈ 0; retry justified with k_op ≪ k_cl "so U = C". Same omission of k_ch as on 2026-10-14.

misconceptions.claim: Matching the coefficients of v_1 and v_2 on both sides of ṗ = pQ is justified by the linearity of pQ.
misconceptions.truth: Linearity only splits pQ into c_1(v_1Q) + c_2(v_2Q); matching coefficients is justified by linear independence of the v_i (unique expansion).

evidence.note: Completion problem at 70% confidence: gave 'linearity of pQ' as the reason for equating v_2 coefficients.
Unprompted, named linear independence of the v_i (with V square) as what makes V invertible in Q = V^{-1}ΛV. Adjacent use of independence, not the coefficient-matching step itself.

goals.title: Mathematical toolkit

milestones.title: Approximation craft: expand in the right small parameter and know when it fails
milestones.description: Done = with explicit remainders/orders, derive the EX2 limit, the harmonic approximation of a potential well, and Verlet's local/global error order; say when each breaks.

milestones.title: Derive the horizontal-shift identity for two uptake curves, ∫(g−f) d ln t = ∫_0^N ln(t_g/t_f) dd, via Fubini and Frullani, and prove the truncation error bound
milestones.description: On paper: inverse of a monotone uptake curve, area read horizontally (Fubini), Frullani for e^{-at}-e^{-bt} over t, then the sandwich bound P_min ≤ t_g/t_f ≤ P_max and the truncation bound (d_1+(N-d_2))/N · ln(P_max/P_min). Extension: moments and the Jensen sign of the pointwise error.

milestones.title: Derive Stirling and the thermodynamic limit by Laplace's method
milestones.description: Done = Stirling with first correction derived; explain why free energy is dominated by the saddle.

milestones.title: Derive PCA as SVD of centered data and run it on a trajectory
milestones.description: Done = spectral theorem stated/proved for symmetric matrices, PCA = SVD derived, applied to real MD coordinates.

milestones.title: Derive gradients of matrix expressions
milestones.description: Done = linear-layer backprop, softmax Jacobian, least-squares normal equations derived and checked numerically.

milestones.title: Prove the CLT via cumulant generating functions; isotope envelope as example
milestones.description: Done = CLT via cumulants; isotope envelope computed via generating functions and its Gaussian limit.

milestones.title: Bayesian inference from scratch: conjugacy, Metropolis MCMC, hierarchical models, evidence
milestones.description: Done = Metropolis sampler written and validated; a hierarchical model fit; two models compared by evidence/Laplace approximation.

milestones.title: Markov chains and Markov reward processes
milestones.description: Done = detailed balance, stationary distribution, spectral gap -> relaxation times; Bellman equation derived and value iteration implemented.

milestones.title: Derive Fokker-Planck from Langevin and show Boltzmann is stationary
milestones.description: Done = Ornstein-Uhlenbeck solved, FP derived, Itô vs Stratonovich explained.

milestones.title: Derive Boltzmann as maximum entropy; KL, Gibbs inequality, mutual information
milestones.description: Done = max-ent derivation with Lagrange multipliers; KL >= 0 proved; MI computed for a toy.

milestones.title: Convexity, duality, and gradient-descent stability
milestones.description: Done = Lagrange dual of a simple problem; GD step-size bound from Hessian eigenvalues derived and demonstrated.

milestones.title: Large deviations: Cramér via Chernoff, rate function as Legendre transform, Gärtner-Ellis
milestones.description: Done = rate function of a sample mean derived; Legendre/SCGF link explained; connection to free energy made.

milestones.title: Derive Jarzynski and Crooks and the LDT view of work distributions
